business_problem: McKesson had to meet new pharmaceutical traceability regulations at extreme scale, but its monolithic Postgres and SAP environment could not reliably handle the serialization, verification, and latency demands of the DSCSA deadline.
solution_summary: McKesson redesigned its pharmaceutical traceability stack around MongoDB Atlas to separate massive serialization workloads from the rest of its legacy supply-chain systems. Instead of forcing DSCSA traffic through a monolithic Postgres and SAP environment, the team created a Distributed Serial Repository to absorb verification calls from 60 warehouses and a Central Data Repository to manage downstream data for more than 350,000 customers per day. Atlas became the unified document database behind both systems because its flexible model matched the hierarchical structure of DSCSA records and could run across cloud and on-prem environments. Internal benchmarks verified that Atlas could handle the real-time verification load, while integrated services simplified development and operations. The new architecture centralizes serialization data, authenticates prescription containers back to manufacturers, and gives McKesson a scalable core for compliance and future AI use cases.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Provides the scalable document database foundation for McKesson's serial-verification and central data repositories.

data_flow: Serialization and verification events from 60 warehouses flow into MongoDB Atlas-backed repositories, where hierarchical DSCSA records are processed and matched to manufacturer traceability data before authenticated results are served to McKesson's downstream customer and supply-chain workflows.
business_outcome: McKesson met the DSCSA deadline, absorbed a 300x demand spike without service disruption, and created a compliant foundation that protects patient safety while supporting future innovation.
